title: Praying the Psalms
blurb: Learn many ways of praying through eight psalms: delight, wonder, trust, repentance, longing, refuge, lament and searching.

steps.title: Delight in the Law
steps.intro: The Psalter opens with a blessing on the one who delights in the Lord's law and meditates on it day and night, rooted like a tree beside streams of water.

quote.text: He meditates on the law because he loves it, and he loves it because he meditates on it.

steps.question: What passage of Scripture could you return to each day this week and slowly make your own?

steps.title: Praise and Wonder
steps.intro: Looking at the heavens, the psalmist marvels that God cares for human beings and has given them a place of honor within creation.

quote.text: If, dearly beloved, we comprehend faithfully and wisely the beginning of our creation, we shall find that man was made in God’s image, to the end that he might imitate his Creator, and that our race attains its highest natural dignity, by the form of the Divine goodness being reflected in us, as in a mirror.

steps.question: When did you last stop to wonder at creation, and what did it lead you to say to God?

steps.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
steps.intro: The best-known psalm of trust pictures God as a shepherd who guides, restores and protects, and as a host who spreads a table for his guest.

quote.text: He hath brought me forth in the narrow ways, wherein few walk, of His righteousness; not for my merit’s sake, but for His Name’s sake.

steps.question: Where do you most need to trust the Shepherd to lead you, even through a dark valley?

steps.title: Have Mercy on Me
steps.intro: Traditionally linked to David after his sin, this penitential psalm asks God for mercy, cleansing and a new heart and steadfast spirit.

quote.text: Let them seek a little mercy of Thee, that have sinned in ignorance: “Have pity,” he saith, “upon me, after Thy great mercy.” Relieve a deep wound after Thy great healing.

steps.question: What would you ask God to wash, heal or renew in you? Put it in your own words.

steps.title: My Soul Thirsts
steps.intro: From a dry and weary land, the psalmist longs for God like a thirsty body and finds in his love something better than life.

quote.text: For there are two kinds of compunction, as you know: one that is afraid of eternal pains, the other that sighs for heavenly rewards; since the soul that is athirst for God is first moved to compunction by fear, and afterwards by love.

steps.question: What are you thirsting for most, and is it the same as what you are praying for?

steps.title: Under His Wings
steps.intro: This psalm of refuge promises that the one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will be protected, and that God's angels will guard his steps.

quote.text: He says this, that thy protection may not be to thee from thyself, that thou mayest not imagine that thou canst defend thyself; He will defend thee, to deliver thee from the hunter’s snare, and from an harsh word.

steps.question: What danger or worry do you need to place under God's protection rather than your own?

steps.title: Out of the Depths
steps.intro: One of the penitential psalms, it cries to the Lord from the depths, trusts in his forgiveness, and waits for him like watchmen waiting for the morning.

quote.text: Whence doth he cry? From the deep. Who is it then who crieth? A sinner. And with what hope doth he cry? Because He who came to absolve from sins, gave hope even to the sinner down in the deep.

steps.question: What is the "deep" you are crying from? Say it plainly to God, as the psalmist does.

steps.title: You Search Me and Know Me
steps.intro: The psalmist realizes that God knows his sitting and rising, his thoughts and words, and that there is nowhere he can flee from God's presence.

quote.text: At length, miserable runaway, thou hast learnt, that by no means canst thou make thyself far from Him, from whom thou hast wished to remove far away.

steps.question: What would it be like to stop hiding from the God who already knows you completely?
